classification.difficultyReason: Recognise reflection and rotation equivalence and count separate cases according to repeated colours.

content.prompt:
With an unlimited supply of six different coloured pop-sticks, you want to make as many different coloured equilateral triangles as possible. Two triangles have the same colouring if one is a reflection or rotation of the other. For example, the triangles below have the same colouring.

How many different ways can the triangles be coloured?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 9, reflected triangle pair in the upper right column
spec.description: Two upright equilateral triangles in a horizontal pair. The left triangle has orange left edge, blue right edge and red base. The right triangle swaps the orange and blue edges and retains the red base.
spec.mathematics: The two colourings are equivalent under reflection; the three edge colours are distinct.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied example, visible in the question edition.

answer.short:
56.

Count colourings with one, two or three distinct colours.
answer.worked:
Rotations and reflections of an equilateral triangle allow every permutation of its three edges, so only the colours selected and their multiplicities matter.

All three edges the same colour: $6$ choices.

Exactly two colours: choose the repeated colour in $6$ ways and the other colour in $5$ ways, giving $6\times5=30$ choices.

Three different colours: $\binom{6}{3}=20$ choices.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Total colourings}&=6+6\times5+\binom{6}{3}\\\text{Total colourings}&=6+30+20\\\text{Total colourings}&=56.\end{align*}$$
